primitives.name: Collective Instinctual Persistence
primitives.verbatim_quote: 423 though a collection of any given thing—like postage-stamps —need not be begun by any given person, yet the chances are that if accidentally it be begun by a person with the collecting instinct, it will probably be continued.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C(t)': 'collection state at time t (dimensionless)', 'I': 'instinctual predisposition (dimensionless)', 'P(C|I)': 'probability of continuation given instinct (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Instinctual initiation is probabilistic; continuation depends on initial condition and temporal persistence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P(C|I) approaches zero, collection ceases.

layer2.mapping: Stochastic process with absorbing barrier at termination; GSI models P(C|I); GSE models C(t) evolution.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of collection initiation and continuation rate.

primitives.name: Possession-Based Motivation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The chief interest of the objects, in the collector's eyes, is that they are a collection, and that they are his.
primitives.assumptions: Ownership and collection completeness drive motivational strength; M = f(O, C).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When O = 0 or C → 0, M vanishes.

layer2.mapping: Motivational kernel derived from possession operator; GSI computes M; GSE maps to behavioral state.
layer2.telemetry: Self-reported ownership satisfaction and collection completeness metrics.

primitives.name: Social Contagion in Acquisition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Boys will collect anything that they see another boy collect, from pieces of chalk and peach-pits up to books and photographs.
primitives.assumptions: Acquisition actions propagate through social networks with delay T; S modulates A.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S → 0, A becomes independent of social input.

layer2.mapping: Contagion model with threshold dynamics; GSI encodes S; GSE simulates A propagation.
layer2.telemetry: Peer-acquisition correlation and temporal spread rate.

The primitives define acquisition dynamics through three core mechanisms: instinctual persistence, possession-based motivation, and social contagion. Instinctual persistence models how collections begin and continue based on individual predisposition, forming a stochastic process with memory. Possession-based motivation links ownership and completeness to motivational intensity, creating a derived kernel for decision-making. Social contagion captures how acquisition behaviors spread among peers, modeled as a thresholded influence network. These interact to form a multi-layered system where GSI infers latent instigating factors and GSE predicts behavioral evolution. Failure modes include loss of instinct, disconnection from ownership, and breakdown of social influence, each leading to cessation of collection activity.
